To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two new cloning vectors have been constructed by in vitro recombinant techniques.
two new cloning vehicles were constructed by in vitro recombinant experiments involving restriction endonuclase fragments from the plasmid pBRL22 and the plasmid PBR325.
the plasmids we constructed are useful for cloning DNA fragments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new set of cloning vehicles, which are characterized by their high copy number and their ability to replicate autonomously in Escherichia coli.
the construction of cloning vectors that have unique restriction sites in the ampi- cillin and/or tetracycline genes and unique sites in the chlor- amphenicol gene.
the development of new cloning vectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pBR322 plasmid is a useful cloning vector for in vitro experiments involving restriction endo- nuclease fragments of 200 to 1000 bp.
pBR328 is an excellent vector for the cloning of DNA fragments in Escherichia coli, which can be used for the construction of hybrid plasmids and the subsequent analysis of the cloned DNA.
the pBR322, pBR325, pBR327 and pBR328 plamids are all suitable for cloning experiments in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed two new plasmids which contain unique sites for a large number of restriction enzymes.
we have now developed a series of plasmid vectors which contain unique sites for 14 restriction enzymes and which are compatible with each other.
pBR327 can be used to clone EcoRI fragments up to 1.1 kbp and pBR328 can be used for cloning EcoRI fragments up 1.8 kbp.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pBR327 and pBR328 plas- mids can be used for cloning DNA fragments that have been cut with any of the restriction enzymes mentioned above, or any combination thereof, and that these plasmids are suitable for the construction of in vitro recombinant molecules containing multiple DNA inserts.
the new plasmid pbr328 has unique restriction sites in each antibiotic resistance gene and can be used to clone DNA fragments up to 4900 bp in size.
the new vectors are useful tools for the construction of new cloning vehicles, and for the study of the mechanisms of plasmid replication and maintenance.
